01_bm25.text: Beware of Essential and how it does business. I am extremely disappointed in the Essential PH-1 phone and the company's support model. I bought the PH-1 phone from Amazon who only sells it via third party resellers as Essential the company does not directly sell their phone through Amazon. Within two weeks, the PH-1 camera stops working so I contacted Essential for support. Keep in mind that Essential sells phones but does not have a phone number to contact them for support. They only communicate through email. I describe the problem to them and they request additional information from me: my name, address, proof of purchase, serial number, etc. After providing them with all the data, they inform me that they will not support me because I bought the phone from a reseller. They said they only support the phone if it is bought directly from Essential and Amazon.

It fits excellent in the hand and is a perfect replacement to my Nexus 5x. Hands down the best-designed phone I've ever owned. Migrated to the PH-1 as a former Samsung flagship owner (most recently the S6 Edge), preceded by a Nexus and a Motorola. People close to me have owned iPhones and Samsungs, which I've played around with frequently, so I've had a good sampling of the flagship products for the past several years. I'll say that, unequivocally, the Essential PH-1 is the best-designed phone I've ever owned, by a wide margin. As noted by many others, its industrial design and overall 'feel' is second-to-none. This thing is an absolute joy to use. Once in a blue moon I'm lucky enough to buy something that delights me every time I use it, see it, or pick it up; the PH-1 is exactly such a thing. I read widely about the phone before purchasing it, and the negative reviews made me sufficiently leery to cancel my pre-order.
And in the end you'll be holding what the Essential PH-1 was always meant to be. A love letter to the industry, now at half the price. Hope this helps! Take care!

Also bear in mind a lot of reviewers tend to parrot older criticisms that predate Essentials many updates. It's quite conceivable that with everything Essential is doing, in a month or two Essential Phone PH-1 could well be as good or better than many of its $1000 competitors.
In just 12 months. In just 12 months my Essential Phone PH - 1 has stopped running. The screen of the smartphone is black. Even if you press the power button, nothing responds.

Absolutely love this phone!. I'm extremely happy with the Essential ph-one. I'm rooting for this company to make it and would definitely continue to purchase from them in the future if they were to come out with an "Essential ph-two" (I think they kind of painted them self in a corner there lol. )

This is really impressive. Essential published the December security update at the very same day as Google did for their Pixel 2 phones. No other company did this. And everything looks extremely promising for future updates - The Essential PH-1 has an open Android 8.0 beta test with detailed instructions for manual installation, covered under warranty. Reports say that the software experience is further improved even in the beta version. - The Essential PH-1 will get hardware abstraction layers (HALs) for much easier and faster updates (Project Treble). While all phones that are released with Android 8 or newer are required to implement Treble, phones updated to Android 8 can choose if they want to support it. Essential is one of only three companies that confirmed Treble support. All the big players will not add support to old phones.

Seriously.) With all this, if there is never a PH-2 made, I will be extremely disappointed. Hopefully, after skipping a cycle, Essential is able to get back on their feet and crank out a successor to the PH-1, with better day-one support and, as difficult as it may be, even further refinement to what I consider to be perhaps the quintessential Android phone. I'll be in line to buy it.

The camera quality is pretty decent, definitely not as bad as the initial complaints, and for casual use I haven't had any problems with picture quality. The only 2 caveats I have that make this 4 stars instead of a perfect 5 stars are: 1) the signal reception is sometimes weak, and that is arguably the most important part of a phone; and 2) Essential will probably not exist as a company for much longer in their current form, so although they have committed to updates for a while there is still some doubts about their future. The main competitor to the Essential PH-1 that I considered was the OnePlus 6. The Essential PH-1 has not been a disappointment, and I do not regret choosing this phone. It is very good value, especially when it goes for $300 or less.

This phone is for people that want a company that will support their device and their customers, and not lock it down. This is the first generation Essential PH-1, and there have been weird quirks and bugs, and that's to be expected, but Essential has done what no other modern device manufacturer does: updates and customer service. That in itself is work the price that's half of what you'd pay for another "flagship" device.

If you want a pure Android experience, get this phone!. If you are an Android enthusiast, then this phone is for you. It offers a pure Android experience without annoying bloatware and UI overlays found in do many other devices. I have used the Essential PH-1 now for two months and am very satisfied with my decision to go with it. Essential has pushed several updates to the platform that has enhanced performance and stability across nearly all aspects of the phone. The camera app has been greatly improved and performs extremely well compared to the early days of this phone. I have experienced ZERO crashes or feezes through the installed updates. In essence, I recommend the Essential Phone PH-1, especially if you want something different.

The folks at Essential have done a great job at addressing the early release issues. I mean, look for yourself at these pictures taken with the native camera app. Do you see anything wrong? No! It takes incredible shots. If you are on ATT and shopping for an unlocked phone that is truly great, look no further than the Essential PH 1. Nuff said.

A Pleasant Surprise.. I have been following the reviews of/for the Essential PH-1 ever since monthly updates stopped coming to my my favorite Nexus 6. Did not think any of the more expensive devices could ever do a better job with the items I use a phone for than the Nexus. However, the Essential PH-1 is a real deal. Just a tad slimmer that my Nexus, which is great and easier to hold. It updated very quick and fast, and I have not had any of the issues so far that many have complained about. Glad to have made this choice. The 360 camera works flawlessly, and Essential has done a great job in perfecting the external device attachment feature using a magnetic snap on. Added a clear TPU case for a better grip and a bit of protection.

I thought I was paying 3x what I normally pay for a phone to get one that WOULDN'T do this, but I was wrong. I took it in to my carrier who worked on it for about 30 minutes but agreed that it was a problem with the phone itself, not the SIM Card. Even better, I emailed Essential about the problem with no response. Thankfully, the return policy on Amazon allowed me to return it and get a full refund; I used the money to buy a brand-new S7 for less than the PH-1 costs. Excellent phone in need of a successor. This was by far my favorite phone. I broke it by accident so I moved onto the Pixel 3 but if Essential made a successor to the PH-1 I would buy it in a heartbeat. The hardware was such a pleasure and amazing to hold in the hand, too bad it wasn't a success.

If you are planning to buy it, go for it, you won't be disappointed. -Happy customer!

Allot of people sleep on this phone because it had problems & bugs when it first launched. Essential has sorted out the kinks & with it running Android 9.0... your basically getting a Pixel 2 with a 5.8" bezel less screen.

Running a finger across the screen feels SO nice. It’s the nicest touch screen I’ve run my finger across to be honest... so smooth. My finger literally glides across the surface. I don’t use screen protectors any more. Just too much hassle and often times reduced responsiveness. So, with no screen protectors I can say when comparing this to say my S8+, the glass is just less 'tacky'. distinct. powerful. sharp. Bought the ph-1 for prime day but definitely would have paid more for this device. Glad to have the chance to have such a premium phone. The essential is solid in hardware and software. The camera has a lot of potential and even as it is the quality is very good. Hopefully essential will keep improving. The Essential ph-1. I bought this for my son on Prime Day. With a gift card the final price was 209.00. Yikes, to me that was the deal of the year. Anyway, I jumped on the Amazon deal and could not be more happy. I've had the phone since 7/20 and using it as my primary device. A great and unique, well built phone.. I snapped up the Ocean Depths color when they first came out and I'm very pleased with the Essential PH-1. Such well built quality is hard to find. I replaced a Nexus 6, as I wanted as close to a stock Android experience as possible. The PH-1 has delivered, and continues to rollout security/os updates. That said, there are some flaws, inconveniences, and features I miss from my old phone: 1. Wireless signal strength is 15-25% weaker. In some country areas I have no service where my old Nexus 6 and my friends Huawei/Pixel XL have limited coverage. Don't rely on this phone while hiking! 2. Miss the dual front-facing speakers. The volume on the PH-1 is respectable, but it still sounds cheap and holding the phone can get awkward, by comparison. 3. The reflective LED display is annoying in most lighting conditions. Really miss the AMOLED display. 4.

This made the original price tag seem obscene and the phone unrefined. In addition, the camera software was a huge letdown. It is now competitive with the Oneplus 5/5T rather than paling in comparison to the Pixel and iPhone, which are significantly more expensive. That said some folks seem to feel that the Oneplus 5T edges out the Essential PH-1 in a close race. One key thing to consider is Android Oreo. 6 Months Later - Finally worth another look. OVERVIEW I’ve owned more phone that I can count over the years. Since the first Android phones 8+ years ago, to the occasional iPhone, and to my now present daily driver, the Galaxy S8+. I’ll be taking that technical experience to see how the new Essential Phone (PH-1) fares in the competitive smartphone environment. It’s now been about 6 months since the PH-1 was released. It has since had a $200 price drop and countless software updates to fix some critical bugs and issues with stability, usability, and the camera. Let’s jump in!

The new portrait feature has been put through the paces on the phone and is a great feature with solid results. At this point, I'd stack the camera on this phone up to almost any phone with the possible exception of Samsung and Pixel. So think about it, there are dozens of other phone manufactures that produce similar if not inferior photo quality to the Essential PH-1. Using the last 6 months as a barometer, the velocity of updates for the camera that we have seen will certain further enhancement photo quality and eliminate all of the concerns for the point and shoot recreational photographer. The bezel-less screen, color contrast, and sharpness are on par with my Apple iPhone. When comparing the screen size to the Apple 8 Plus, the Essential PH-1 has a larger overall useful screen size (eliminating the dead black space around the iPhones's screen).

Essential PH-1 for the win!. This phone is truly something to behold. Everything about it feels well-crafted. In fact, this phone is so good that I paid quite a bit for a like new used one and the prime Day special came out dropping the phone to $250 the day after I received it and I'm not even mad! Incredible product!

Flagship phone with midrange price. It`s a pretty solid device all around. Build and display really pushes this thing to the next level. It's so different, that people have stopped me to ask what phone it was. I'm on Oreo 8.1 Beta 1 and I haven't really seen the problems that others have talked about yet. I'm coming from a 6P, so I'm missing the stereo speakers, but the PH-1 gets pretty loud without getting tinny on the higher end, which is pretty nice. Battery is great: +6 hours SOT! Personally, I find the camera more than serviceable. Essential's own app is great for Mono photos, but I threw a Google Camera port onto it, and the pictures come out as good as the 6P easily. That's no question. Essential's own stock app is much better than it was before. It's not the hardware that's buggered up, it's the software; the hardware is pretty good.

The camera does do decent pictures but can do more in my opinion. Official Lineage was being developed but they hit a road block so perhaps the actual essential devs could assist as having the option of official Lineage would be a game changer. The unofficial works pretty good an hats off to invisiblek for his efforts. Good buy at under $300 new as your essentially getting pixel 2 spec brand new with a less capable camera which I hope gets an overhaul with Android Q! which is coming out for the PH-1.

In conclusion, despite the few shortcomings, I LOVE this phone. I haven't had any of the maddening issues that some have had, and my phone has performed exceedingly well. I would be willing to say the this has taken the place of my favorite smartphone that I've ever owned, and even if Essential doesn't do a PH-2, I feel confident they will continue to support this phone for a long time. I'll be running this one until it gives out on me.

Could this essentially be your next phone?. This has potential to be the essential phone it could be. I think that at this price point its close to the best phone you can buy. The specs are flagship quality with that beast of a qualcomm snapdragon 835 chip paired with 4gb of RAM to make apps buttery smooth and transitions seamless. The Essential just got version 9 the same day as the Pixel. That's incredible. (I will add more about Android 9 once I have had a chance to play with it on the PH-1). Very pleased with this purchase.

Essential Phone: One of the best devices of early 2018!!! Design on this thing is incredible!! Buy it!. The Essential Phone has a lot of polarizing views. I will try to give an updated and honest opinion. I am a tech junkie and review phones as a hobby. I try not to spend more than $400-500 on devices and sometimes much less. I feel that spending close to $1000 for a device I will keep for maybe a year is a waste of money. I also find it a lot harder for companies to offer a truly great device in the mid range price bracket than the top end. It is easy to dazzle when money is not an issue yet even then most devices fail in one way or another. Can the Essential phone really compete with the big guys and are all the negative reviews true? Should I buy a PH-1 when the company is developing a PH-2?

Big screen, small phone.. I'm really digging my new PH-1, had a little trouble with convincing local Verizon that they supported it. Also for some reason we had to place the SIM card in another phone, get it on the network, then take it out and put into the Essential. Otherwise for a last minute Amazon Prime Day purchase it's been a good deal. $249 on Prime Day.

Update: Over a year later and my PH-1 is still going strong. Even better, all of the old bugs were worked out and it's running the newest version of Android like a champ! Photos look great, and the phone is responsive and lasts a long time on a charge. I'm very pleased, and bumping the review up to five stars because Essential kept at it and did what they needed to in order for this phone to be a real winner.

Think of the Essential PH-1 as the new Sony PlayStation 5, rushed to the public with only 1 or two game titles, Pong being one of them; yes, it would disappointment, but given time to refine and update the release of new software and it will blow everything out of the water because the Hardware is "there"... There is no other device in the market that matches the choice of materials, build quality or design aesthetic. The software experience will improve regularly, and with Essential supporting the ROM community by releasing their Kernel Source, you can bet the sky will be the limit... so ignore the Camera, ignore the lean, lackluster software, ignore the yet to be experienced "lag" or "lock-ups".

In summary, it's not a perfect device, but excellent hardware coupled with "pure" Android leave the PH-1 with a lot going for it. Amazing phone! The reconditioned phone I received looks/functions like a brand new phone.. I was very interested in the Essential PH-1 when it first hit the market, but wasn't very interested in the phone's initial price. It seems that the phone has fallen out of favor with critics and tech reviewers, but in my opinion, this is a fantastic phone. I purchased the reconditioned PH-1 after the screen on my Pixel shattered. The reconditioned phone arrived in less than 48 hours, and was ready to make a call within 5 minutes of installing my old SIM and powering the phone up. It downloaded the Android 9 (Pie) update within the first 10 minutes, and I was good to go. It seems that the phone I received (and based on forum posts, the phones most people receive) was setup for Sprint.

I value a stock Android OS experience over features like storage, camera specifications. I value a stock Android OS experience over features like storage, camera specifications, and screen resolution. I'm happy to say I can get my stock Android experience without sacrificing overmuch with this phone. The PH-1 is not top-of-the-line in many respects but for the price point it is an exceptional piece of equipment. Android users who are migrating or upgrading from the old Nexus or current Pixel lineup would do well to take the PH-1 for a test drive. I like mine a lot.

Additionally, I have a negative perspective on "renting" a phone from my provider (AT&T,) so I tend to purchase my phone outright. The recent price reduction (~$330) on the Essential PH-1 made it properly appealing, though I could still kick myself for missing out when it was priced at $250 during Prime Day. Suffice it to say that I will update this review as I learn its pros, its cons, and where the compromises are. [Update]: I have been able to provide some selective updates in the categories below, as I have had this now almost a week. I expect to have more updates in the near future, when\where warranted. There have however been articles stating that the company is in financial trouble. If true support for this phone could end abruptly if the company goes under. Over all the phone is very snappy. It fit the bill almost perfectly for me. A very powerful phone at a low price. It has a few minor drawbacks but overall I am very satisfied with my purchase.
Great phone. This phone has been fantastic. Great battery life. Great display. It's fast and the camera is great. Not to mention 128 gb standard storage. It's great value for money.

The display is approx the same size as our previous phones but the overall phone dimensions are smaller, making it better for handling. We have more memory left over in the Essential Phone (128 Gig) and without a Micro SD card, the phone appears faster than our Moto's with 64 Gig Micro SD cards. Instead of paying almost $1000 for the latest phone with a Snapdragon 845, I get 2 phones that "I feel" is just as fast for the same price of 1 with Snapdragon 835 on the Essential Phone, which we consider very fast! I read ALL the reviews but so far, we have been pleasantly surprised and incurred none of the problems others may speak of! If things change, I'll do an update.
My favorite Android phone. One of the best unlocked cell phones we own. Fast, well built, great display, long battery life, several of my friends are buying this phone after seeing it.

Very good purchase. Fast review first week of use(pros for me) : -Amazing design and materials! -250$? really good deal smile -Performance outstanding -Pure android -the best screen ratio on the market over newer devices -128gb HD

Great specs for the price but know what you're buying.. Update: Had to return my original phone due to grill issues. The new phone doesn't have any issues physically but i had to reset it a few times already due to crashes or hang ups. It's getting quite annoying. Also, the GPS on here is wonky when using Google Maps. It's all over the place. ------------------ Great specs. Everything negative about the phone is true but it's really not all that bad since essential is providing updates constantly. Camera app needs fixing among other things but the display, the built, the size... it's a pretty phone and a good deal especially if you got in on the Black Friday deal. The finger print sensor is super sensitive. Very slippery without a case. It fell off my night stand a few times. About 2.5' drop onto carpet. No damage fortunately. Get a case or a skin at least.

Decent phone with premium feel but with compromises. I purchased this phone as a replacement for my Nexus 6; while I really liked the Nexus 6 and the "pure" Android experience, it was long in the tooth and due for an upgrade. Keep in mind that I only picked this up -after- the price reduction from the initial price so I am reviewing it with that price in mind. TL;DR: Pros: Display, size, storage, Android updates (supposedly - still no 8.0 OTA) Cons: No headphone jack, camera, slippery body, display (if you hate the notch) The display is eye catching and the feel in the hand is premium. It's smaller than the N6 but also heavier on account of the ceramic & titanium build. While the ceramic feels nice it's as slippery as ice. I don't mean this as an analogy, I found the coefficient of static friction in testing to be a little under 0.08.

It can't generate the totally black blacks of this year's OLED phones or an LG C7 television... but make no mistake, this screen is still a quality performer. The blacks are as good as it's going to get on an LCD display, and I could only truly appreciate the contrast differences when I put it next to a Galaxy S8 (I haven't used an iPhone X yet), and it looks better than an iPhone 7 screen. The camera notch at the top didn't bother me 99% of the time, the only time it became annoying was on certain web pages with unique formatting where the whole page fit on one screen and it just cut off a word/link from a menu that I had a hard time selecting. The internals are solid with 128GB of storage and the current flavor of high-end Snapdragon processor with 4GB of RAM.

BMW at a Ford price. Beautiful piece of hardware, very smooth performance, great display. I love the pure Android experience, light, quick and simple. Battery life is good. I would have given it 5 stars except for the lack of headphone jack and it's not waterproof. When I update to a new phone again in about two years, I will be looking forward to seeing Essential's offerings at that time.

What a fantastic thing to be running the latest without having to beg and wait. If there's going to be the Essential Ph2, sign me up! PS - I got mine in exclusive Amazon grey color. The feel of the matte ceramic back is fantastic. The worst thing so far with the initial experience is the screen wall paper. Came with some of the ugliest ever. Who chose these?

great phone. I've had this phone for about 6 months and I love it. Great battery life, excellent camera, beautiful display, and good call quality. Essential will be my first choice for my next phone - if they ever release one!

PROS: + high resolution display – everything looks crisp and clean, very sharp. + very responsive touchscreen with snappy haptic feedback + speaker is LOUD – great for your reality TV-inspired speakerphone calls and for casual gaming + hardware is high-quality and doesn't show its age at all – all tasks are executed smoothly and easily, apps load in a second. + *for me, personally* phone is a little smaller than the current "phablet"-sized phones that I can't tuck away into my pocket. Easily can fit into the pocket of your pants/jeans. CONS: - battery life just isn't that great. Expect to charge your phone every single day, maybe even twice a day on occasion if you're using it a lot. My previous phone, which was a Motorola, could go an entire day, sometimes even two, without needing to be recharged.

Falling apart. Screen scratches and the edges chip very easily. the small glass filled plastic frame around the screen crumbles and now the whole display is coming loose from the titanium frame. What good is a titanium frame and ceramic back when the ceramic is so slippery it sends your phone for a crash landing and the screen and surround are so wimpy they scratch and crack?

The “flaws” I don’t care much about (I call them SMART TRADE-OFFS) ( + / — ) Camera/Picture quality (good enough for me), ( + / — ) Not for VR (still a “niche” use case), ( + / — ) Not waterproof (I don’t swim with my phone), ( + / — ) No headphone jack (I love USB-C), ( + / — ) Weak built-in speaker (I use a headset or an actual high quality speaker when I need good/loud sound), ( + / — ) Unclear whether front facing camera will enable advanced face recognition use cases (the future is coming but I live in the present) The things I wish it did better (or “Why not a 5 star rating”) ( — ) I’d like the screen to be brighter / colors to be more vivid.
I love the big screen. I love the big screen! No borders at all. Can't be used with one hand though. Good quality camera and the developers do a great job updating it constantly.

And now the not so great: - Both cameras are mediocre at best. You can improve image quality somewhat by downloading the Pixel's camera app from XDADevelopers or a similar site, but it's still only a moderate improvement. If high photo quality is important to you, avoid this phone. - The screen digitizer seems like a bottom of the barrel unit. For anyone not familiar, the digitizer is what allows the screen to register your finger touching the display so you can interact with your phone. So ya, its a pretty crucial component. And Essential seems to have cut some corners here. The screen routinely misses my finger pressing on the screen. I would say about 1 out of ever 20-25 touches of the screen simply don't register (for instance, tapping on the screen to launch an app, click on a link, etc).

I heard it often enough that it bothered me. The screen is marketed as a "full screen" which it is when you are just looking at the home screen, but as soon as you go into any app or webpage, the only visible part of screen is below the front facing camera, so your actual usable screen is smaller and not "full screen". The reception also seems to be really bad. I would drop calls, or have to walk outside my office to get any kind of reception. I switched phones, and the reception is much better now. I have returned this phone, and I hope that in the future it gets better, I may try it again. But for now, I picked up a Huawei Mate 9, and for the short time I have had it, I like that much more.
Works like a charm. Camera is not bad at all, after updating to Android 8.1.. [[ASIN:B078SQ7GWK Essential Phone in Halo Gray - 128 GB Unlocked Titanium and Ceramic phone with Edge-to-Edge Display]]

The device is great. I love the flat glass screen it feels .... I did not get the Essential Device from Amazon. I got it from the company itself. The device is great. I love the flat glass screen it feels much better than a curved screen. It does not get very bright outdoors but it does pretty well and the screen to body ratio is fantastic. The build is the best part for me of the device. I is made of titanium sides and a ceramic back. IN MY OPINION it is the best built device out there period. Nothing touches it. Camera is decent. Takes good photos but its definitely not the best. Software is basically vanilla android but the Essential team seems to be very receptive and pushes updates regularly. My problem is with the weak antenna. Using it on At&t my signal would be all over the place.

Great phone, terrible camera. I have been using this device for a few months now. I can say that overall I am very pleased with the look, feel and performance of the phone. I have not had good luck finding a case and screen protector that will work well together, so I have ended up using a wet apply film with no case. I have had many people ask about the phone, the appearance is striking. Maybe it's just being different in an iPhone lemming world, but I think it's a good looking device. The OS is everything is cracked up to be. Lean, minimal and free of crapware. Major win. Security patches have been delivered reliably with no ill effects. The device is responsive and the display is bright with clear, clean color. I have not noticed any difficulty watching anything I wanted. Memory capacity has been more than adequate.

Beautiful. I have a life so I won't write much or do a series of tests so I'll just say it's an amazing phone buy it you won't be upset. Notice no difference than Pixel or s8 other than better looking screen and not completely waterproof.

I do like the screen - plenty bright, great resolution and the notch doesn't bother me at all. Not equal to a good amoled panel, however. UI is clean, as you would expect with a pure Android build, but I kind of miss some of the bells and whistles that other flagship phones might have. Scrolling as quick, but not super smooth. Occasional system stutters. No wireless charging, but has rapid charging available via Power Delivery protocol, which isn't as popular as Quick Charage 2.0/3.0. And you'll need the charger- often, as battery life on this phone is abysmal. No headphone jack, but that isn't a big deal - all phones are going in that direction. Recent upgrade brought bluetooth 5.0, but on this phone, range is very limited and it seems to suck more power than it should.

I also encounter various issues such as noticeable weaker signal reception, the signal could drop and back in a second. also google voice dictation not work, not able to pick up my voice may be related to the second mic located at the back. As first, I wanted to accept these various issues as no phone is perfect. I really like the phone. When I finally wanted to pull the trigger to reset or wipe data to see those issue can be fixed, it is too late. The phone keeps reboot and reboot, no display, ... dead. I contacted both Amazon and Essential and understand I have 2 options. Return for a partial refund (maybe 80% as pass the return period) Or get a replacement from Essential. I struggled and realised it is not easy to say goodbye.
